starterFiles.name: README.md
starterFiles.text:
# Dispatch Ledger Service

Offline synthetic order-to-fulfillment service for reproducible agent benchmarking. Node24, no external dependencies or services. `npm test` runs the supplied regression tests. Start with `TASK.md`, `ACCEPTANCE.md`, and `context/00-index.md`.

- `src/orders/`: creation, query, DTO and durable projection.
- `src/storage/`: shared journal and deterministic failure hooks.
- `src/fulfillment/`: downstream idempotency, recovery and holds.
- `src/billing/`: invoice export and pagination.
- `src/auth/`, `src/audit/`, `src/domain/`: permissions, audit schema and validation/money.
- `src/api/`: thin in-process HTTP-shaped routes.
- `test/`: existing regressions; add `test/added-*.test.mjs` for this change.
- `context/`: current contracts, superseded decisions, incident evidence and frozen external-style references.

The journal and delivery sink intentionally persist across new service instances. They are local stand-ins for real service boundaries, not claims of database or network realism.

starterFiles.name: context/00-index.md
starterFiles.text:
# Context map and authority
Synthetic, frozen benchmark evidence. No document describes an actual company incident.

## AUTHORITY-1
Use current contracts and requirements dated 2026-10-20 over historical ADRs. Incident observations establish only the fixture mechanism, not production frequency or financial impact. Historical documents remain available to explain misleading assumptions. No live web or MCP lookup is needed.

Read current requirements, trace relevant code, then use incident evidence to resolve a causal hypothesis. Do not alter context files. The service baseline is intentionally incomplete for the task; the documents are the requirements.

Internal nodes: API, storage, security, workflow, audit, incident logs and historical decisions. External-style nodes: the frozen delivery-provider contract and integer-money guide, supplied locally to avoid time-dependent retrieval.

starterFiles.name: context/01-api-contract.md
starterFiles.text:
# Current API contract — 2026-10-20
Owner: service team. Status: authoritative internal contract.

## API-1
createService({journal,sink,clock}) returns createOrder, countOrders, listOrders, getOrder, recover, holdOrder, releaseOrder, exportInvoices and auditEvents. actor={tenantId,permissions}; all data is tenant scoped.

## API-2
createOrder(actor,{key,items:[{sku,quantity,unitCents}],taxBps?,deferFulfillment?}) returns exactly {id,tenantId,key,status:'committed',totalCents,createdAt}. Repeated tenant/key returns the first committed identity even if a different request body arrives; it must not create another durable record. Count committed orders, never attempts. IDs may have gaps. Invalid data is INVALID/400; unauthorized is FORBIDDEN/403. Foreign/missing order IDs are indistinguishable NOT_FOUND/404.

## API-3
Default create attempts fulfillment after commit. deferFulfillment:true skips initial dispatch but recovery may later dispatch it unless held. Post-commit acknowledgement failure may reject the initial call; a retry must recover the committed order and complete pending delivery. listOrders sorts by stable order ID and returns cloned DTOs. No public API field removal or changed error code is allowed.

## API-4
The thin router exposes POST/GET /orders, GET /orders/:id, POST /fulfillment/run, POST /orders/:id/hold and /release, GET /invoices. It maps service errors to their status and unexpected storage failures to STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE/503. It is an in-process HTTP-shaped adapter; no listening socket is required.

starterFiles.name: context/02-storage-contract.md
starterFiles.text:
# Current storage guarantees — 2026-10-20
Owner: storage team. Status: authoritative.

## STORAGE-1
A journal instance persists across simulated service restarts. appendOrder is a legacy nonunique append. commitOrder atomically enforces tenant/key uniqueness at the persistence boundary, after beforeCommit has resolved. Its returned record may be an existing committed order rather than the supplied draft. Do not assume a process-local lookup or service-instance mutex prevents races across service instances.

## STORAGE-2
failNext({key:'tenant:key',phase:'before'|'after'}) injects one deterministic failure. Before means no commit; after means commit happened but its acknowledgement was lost. Neither caller-side rejection nor a missing in-memory cache entry proves rollback. Read durable events to resolve ambiguity.

## STORAGE-3
Projection state derives from committed events. Recovery may reprocess an event multiple times. A journal record for dispatch may be missing after an external delivery; durable downstream idempotency is therefore necessary. Different order keys must make progress while one beforeCommit callback is blocked.

starterFiles.name: context/03-delivery-provider.md
starterFiles.text:
# Frozen delivery provider contract
Synthetic external-style reference, version 2, 2026-10-20.

## DELIVERY-1
createSink() represents a durable external provider retained across service restarts. send(order) creates a new receipt every time. sendOnce(idempotencyKey,order) returns the first receipt for that key without repeating delivery. Bind the key to tenant and committed order identity; do not use an attempt ID.

## DELIVERY-2
Receipt creation is synchronous in this fixture. The boundary stands in for a provider idempotency guarantee, not a distributed transaction with the journal. Repeating recovery and repairing a missing local fulfillment.sent record must not create another external receipt. No production durability or network throughput is inferred.

starterFiles.name: context/04-security.md
starterFiles.text:
# Current security policy — 2026-10-20
Owner: security team. Status: authoritative.

## SECURITY-1
orders:write authorizes create. orders:read authorizes queries, counts and audit queries. fulfillment:write authorizes recovery, hold and release. billing:read alone authorizes invoice export. Never substitute a different permission because a handler is read-only.

## SECURITY-2
Authenticate and authorize before mutating any state or emitting success audit events. A foreign order ID produces NOT_FOUND. Tenant identity participates in idempotency and query filtering. Denied requests leave journal, provider and counters unchanged. Do not leak another tenant's order through invoice pagination or a permissive object lookup.

starterFiles.name: context/05-incident-timeline.md
starterFiles.text:
# Incident evidence — synthetic reproduction INC-42
Observed in deterministic fixture; not production telemetry.

## INCIDENT-1
Two requests for north:k both read an absent projection before either persistence promise resolves. Separate generated IDs are observed in committed events. A sequential retry test did not reveal this interleaving.

## INCIDENT-2
A before-commit timeout left no order.committed event. The active service nevertheless reported one successful order. A later retry increased the reported count again.

## INCIDENT-3
An after-commit timeout left order.committed present but no fulfillment.sent record. The retry returned the cached/projected order without completing delivery. Restart recovery later produced repeated provider receipts because it used a non-idempotent dispatch surface.

## INCIDENT-4
The evidence establishes local causal mechanisms. It does not establish production impact, request frequency, monetary losses or provider outage rates. Preserve this uncertainty explicitly.

context/07-historical-retries.md
starterFiles.text:
# ADR-OLD-1 — retry assumption, 2025-06-01
Status: superseded; retained to explain the old implementation.

An early client assumed any timeout meant storage rolled back. The service counted accepted attempts and relied on an in-memory key lookup. Recovery was assumed to run once.

This ADR is not authoritative. Current STORAGE-1/2/3, API-2/3 and DELIVERY-1/2 replace these assumptions. Do not disable retries to hide a duplicated effect.

starterFiles.name: context/08-holds-requirements.md
starterFiles.text:
# Current fulfillment holds — 2026-10-20
Owner: workflow team. Status: authoritative feature requirements.

## HOLDS-1
holdOrder(actor,{orderId,reason,correlationId}) returns {orderId,held:true}. Require fulfillment:write, same tenant, nonempty reason up to200 characters and correlationId of1–100 characters. A fulfilled order cannot be held (CONFLICT/409). A held order cannot dispatch, including after service restart.

## HOLDS-2
releaseOrder(actor,{orderId,correlationId}) returns {orderId,held:false}. Repeating an already-effective hold or release is a no-op; it emits no additional transition or audit event. Release does not itself send delivery; a subsequent recover may deliver exactly once. Both hold and release must persist as events and reconstruct state after restart. Concurrent calls in this in-process service must not duplicate transitions.

starterFiles.name: context/09-invoice-requirements.md
starterFiles.text:
# Current invoice export — 2026-10-20
Owner: billing team. Status: authoritative feature requirements.

## INVOICE-1
exportInvoices(actor,{cursor?:0,limit?:20,correlationId}) requires billing:read and returns {items,nextCursor}. Each item is {orderId,tenantId,subtotalCents,taxCents,totalCents}. Include only that tenant's committed orders, sorted by stable order ID. Invoice totals are recomputed from committed line items and taxBps.

## INVOICE-2
Integer minor units only. subtotal=sum(quantity*unitCents). Tax is rounded half up once per order: floor((subtotal*taxBps+5000)/10000). E.g.101c at5000bps→51c tax,152c total;1c→1c tax,2c total. No floating currency conversion.

## INVOICE-3
Cursor is a nonnegative integer offset; limit is an integer1–100. nextCursor is null when exhausted, including empty pages. Invalid pagination is INVALID/400, with no success audit. The snapshot is static within each acceptance pagination case; concurrent inserts across pages are outside this task. Every valid export invocation emits one audit event; correlation ID identifies that invocation but is not a deduplication key.

starterFiles.name: context/10-audit-contract.md
starterFiles.text:
# Shared audit schema — 2026-10-20
Owner: platform team. Status: authoritative.

## AUDIT-1
Successful hold.created, hold.released and invoice.exported actions emit {id,action,tenantId,subjectId,correlationId,outcome:'success',at}. Subject is the order ID for a transition and 'invoices' for export. at comes from the injected clock. Retain existing order.created behavior.

## AUDIT-2
Transition and its audit fact are one durable event. No-op holds/releases do not append another event. Failed authorization, validation or nonexistent orders cannot produce success audit. auditEvents(actor) remains tenant scoped. No credentials or request bodies belong in audit facts.

starterFiles.name: context/11-historical-billing.md
starterFiles.text:
# ADR-OLD-2 — prototype invoice export, 2025-10-01
Status: superseded internal experiment.

A prototype exported all tenants to a global dashboard, used orders:read and truncated floating tax fractions. Holds were process-local UI flags. None of these choices is permitted by current SECURITY-1/2, HOLDS-1/2, INVOICE-1/2/3 or AUDIT-1/2.

starterFiles.name: context/12-operations.md
starterFiles.text:
# Operational context
Synthetic internal runbook, 2026-10-20.

## OPS-1
Run npm test from the repository root; dependencies and network are unnecessary. Simulate restart by creating another service with the same journal and sink. beforeCommit can pause one key to expose concurrency. Use fault injection rather than sleeps to model storage ambiguity.

## OPS-2
Do not rewrite the API, delete regressions or add packages. The task is the service core, not a deployment. Native CLI/MCP capabilities may supply file access, but all required task context is already in this repository. Maintain evidence anchors when composing a scoped handoff.

starterFiles.name: context/13-money-reference.md
starterFiles.text:
# Integer-money reference
Synthetic external-style reference, version1, frozen2026-10-20.

## MONEY-1
A basis point is1/10000. Keep integer cents throughout multiplication and addition; ensure intermediate arithmetic stays within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Round tax once per order using the current invoice contract. Signed values, discounts, exchange rates and refunds are outside this fixture.

## MONEY-2
Line quantities1–10000, unitCents0–1000000, taxBps0–10000, at most100 line items. Reject a calculation whose intermediate rounded numerator is not a safe integer. These bounds are validation rules, not measured workloads.

starterFiles.text:
# 2027 roadmap note
Status: draft; not a requirement for these tasks.

## ROADMAP-1
Possible future work: tracking integration, subscriptions, currency conversion, geographic routing and a browser dashboard. Do not implement these in this task. This document deliberately provides plausible but irrelevant context.

# Acceptance contract — incident-recovery

Same contract for every execution approach. Existing context, README.md, package.json, TASK.md, ACCEPTANCE.md and original test/*.test.mjs are frozen; do not change them. Edit src/ and add test/added-*.test.mjs plus the deliverables below. No dependencies or network.

## Functional gates
- One committed tenant/key identity and one delivery for concurrent duplicates.
- Pre-commit failure does not count; post-commit timeout retains durable identity and retry repairs pending delivery.
- Repeated recovery across restart does not duplicate effects; distinct keys make independent progress.
- Existing API, error and tenant behavior remain compatible.

## Required deliverables

- analysis.json with {requirements:[{id,anchors:[...],codePaths:[...],testPaths:[...]}],rejectedHistorical:[...],uncertainty:[...],observedMechanisms:[...]}. Explain the causal sequence in summary.md, including the lost-acknowledgement gap.
- summary.md: changes, evidence-backed explanation, compatibility/migration notes and remaining risks.
- validation.json: {commands:[{command,exitCode}],limitations:[...]}; record actual executed checks. Include npm test.
- Add test/added-*.test.mjs. They must pass on your result and expose at least one task defect/missing behavior on the untouched starter. Do not edit existing regressions.
